An air-gapped AI deployment runs language models, retrieval, and the applications built on them entirely on hardware that has no connection to the internet or to any outside network. Models and updates arrive on approved physical media, nothing phones home, and the organisation carries every operational task a cloud vendor would otherwise handle.

in the usual sense, where servers sit in your own building but can still reach out for model updates, package installs, or licence checks. Plenty of organisations that say “air-gapped” actually mean “on-premise with a strict firewall.” The difference matters, because a true air gapped AI deployment changes how every routine task is done, from installing a library to reading a log.
Keeping it running: updates, patches and monitoring
We’ll map the requirement, size the hardware honestly, and build the update routine your team will run after handover.

It is an AI system - models, retrieval, and applications - running on hardware with no network connection to the internet or any outside network. Software and updates arrive on approved physical media, and nothing in the environment can send data out.

On-premise AI runs on servers you own but usually keeps controlled outbound connectivity for updates, package installs, and vendor support. An air gap removes all outside connectivity, which is stricter and considerably more work to operate.
How do updates and security patches work?

Every update is assembled and tested on a disconnected staging environment outside the gap, written to approved media with checksums, verified on the inside, and installed on a deliberate schedule. The routine should be set up as part of the first deployment.
